title: Fixed-size vectors and matrices of Python user functions as numpy arrays; dot and @ for symbolic vectors and matrices
author: Claude-JG
description: No problem if the access to single items is slower - with numpy, most problems are solved in vectorized form; switch the 3D and 6D vectors to numpy and adapt the scripts that can take the vector form. Symbolic should allow a vectorized form as well: exudyn.symbolic.Vector and Matrix get dot() and the @ operator with numpy's meaning, and numpy defers to them (__array_ufunc__ = None), so that one script computes with numpy arrays and symbolic vectors; * of two symbolic vectors stays the scalar product for now.
releaseNotes: Python user functions get their vectors and matrices of size 3 and 6 as read-only numpy arrays as well, to be used in vectorized form; exudyn.symbolic.Vector and Matrix have dot() and the operator @ with numpy's meaning, and numpy leaves an operation with a symbolic operand to it, so that one function computes with numpy arrays and symbolic vectors
